classification.difficultyReason: Combine triangle angle sums, exterior angles and parallel-line relationships; solve simple equations involving multiples of unknown angles.

content.prompt: Find $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$ in each diagram, giving reasons.

spec.description: Triangle RST with RT extended through T to P; a curved leader identifies the narrow 30-degree angle at R.
spec.mathematics: Angle SRT is 30 degrees, angle RST is 80 degrees, and theta is exterior angle STP.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens and unknown only; no solution.

answer.worked:
An exterior angle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles of $\triangle RST$.
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=30^\circ+80^\circ\\\theta&=110^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle UVW with UW extended to Y and VW extended to X.
spec.mathematics: Angles at U and V are 40 and 100 degrees. Alpha is XWY, vertically opposite UWV.

answer.worked:
Use the angle sum of $\triangle UVW$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle UWV&=180^\circ-40^\circ-100^\circ\\\angle UWV&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\alpha=40^\circ$ because vertically opposite angles at $W$ are equal.

spec.description: Right triangle TBR, with a right-angle square at R.
spec.mathematics: Angles T and B are 3 beta and beta; angle R is 90 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given angle expressions are visible.

answer.worked:
The angles of $\triangle BRT$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}3\beta+\beta+90^\circ&=180^\circ\\4\beta&=90^\circ\\\beta&=22.5^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Right triangle FDE with DF extended through F to X.
spec.mathematics: Angle FDE is 90 degrees, exterior angle XFE is 125 degrees, and FED is gamma.

answer.worked:
Use the exterior angle of $\triangle DEF$.
$$\begin{align*}\gamma+90^\circ&=125^\circ\\\gamma&=125^\circ-90^\circ\\\gamma&=35^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle APQ with B on AP and C on AQ; matching single arrows identify BC parallel to PQ.
spec.mathematics: ACB is 40 degrees, APQ is 70 degrees, and PAQ is theta.
spec.answerVisibility: No inferred angle or solution is shown.

answer.worked:
$\angle ABC=70^\circ$ because corresponding angles are equal when $BC\parallel PQ$.

Use the angle sum of $\triangle ABC$.
$$\begin{align*}\theta+70^\circ+40^\circ&=180^\circ\\\theta&=180^\circ-70^\circ-40^\circ\\\theta&=70^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle JKM with JK extended through K to L.
spec.mathematics: Exterior angle MKL is 140 degrees; interior angles J and M are 2 theta and 3 theta.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original expressions and the exterior-angle given appear.

answer.worked:
Use the exterior angle of $\triangle JKM$.
$$\begin{align*}2\theta+3\theta&=140^\circ\\5\theta&=140^\circ\\\theta&=28^\circ\end{align*}$$
